title_tag: 7 Best Dubai Attraction Passes (2026): Worth It?
meta_description: Dubai Pass, Go City and the hop-on hop-off bundles compared with real math: what the top attractions cost separately vs on a pass, and which pass saves money.
h1_muted: (and When a Pass Is Worth It)
author_role: 7 Dubai attraction passes compared on price, picks, validity and savings vs single tickets
lead: A Dubai attraction pass saves money only if you spend it on the expensive tickets. The 3-pick Dubai Top Attractions Pass (€179) beats buying separately when you choose Burj Khalifa, Aquaventure and IMG Worlds: those three cost €209.27 on their own, so you keep €30.56. Swap IMG for the €13 Dubai Frame and the same pass costs you €19.71 more than single tickets.

Not chasing the big parks? The 5-day hop-on hop-off pass with Lost World Aquarium and Dubai Frame (€63) is the best-rated deal here at 4.4 out of 5, and it costs less than a 1-day bus-and-aquarium ticket plus a Frame entry bought separately.

What decides it: how many paid attractions you will really fit into the validity window (7 days on most passes, 30 on Go City), whether your must-sees are on the list (the €409 Unlimited pass has no IMG Worlds), and the ratings, which are low for this category: four of the seven passes score under 4 out of 5. Below, each pass has its math worked out against single tickets.

review: This is the pass most people mean when they search for the Dubai Pass: one price, then 3, 5 or 7 picks from a list of 38 attractions over 7 days. The list is the strongest on the page because it holds all three of the city's priciest single tickets: At the Top Burj Khalifa, Atlantis Aquaventure and IMG Worlds of Adventure, plus Wild Wadi, Legoland, Motiongate, Ski Dubai, iFly and La Perle.

The math works only when you aim high. Bought separately, a Level 124/125 Burj Khalifa ticket (€69.01), an Aquaventure day pass (€76.96) and IMG Worlds (€63.30) total €209.27. The 3-pick pass is €178.71, so you keep €30.56. Spend one of the three picks on the Dubai Frame (€13.03) and the separate total drops to €159.00, which makes the pass €19.71 dearer. One guest put it plainly: check the attraction prices and pick the most expensive ones.

The catches are practical. You need the Smartvisit app to reserve time slots, some venues still swap the pass for a paper ticket at the counter, and attractions can drop off the list (a 2023 review of the sister Select pass mentions Wild Wadi disappearing before a trip). The 3.9 out of 5 rating reflects that friction rather than the price. For the headliners, it is still the best-value flexible pass here.

review: This is the one pass on the page that clearly saves money without any careful picking. For €62.78 (down from €74) you get 5 consecutive days of Big Bus hop-on hop-off rides on the Red City route and the Blue Beach route, plus entry to the Dubai Frame and The Lost World Aquarium at Atlantis.

Put it next to the one-day alternative. The City Sightseeing 1-day bus with Lost World Aquarium costs €51.06; add a €13.03 Dubai Frame ticket and you are at €64.09 for a single day of buses. This pass is €1.31 cheaper and gives you four more days of transport between Downtown, the Creek souks, Madinat Jumeirah and the Palm.

The limits are about scope and speed. There is no Burj Khalifa, water park or theme park in it, so pair it with a Burj Khalifa ticket if the tower is on your list. Buses run roughly every 60 minutes, and both attraction tickets must be collected from staff at specific stops before you visit. For a relaxed first trip, though, it is the best-rated and simplest deal here.

review: The Select pass is the same Smartvisit system as the Top Attractions Pass, cut down to three picks, one from each pool, for €133.12. Pool 1 holds the expensive tickets (At the Top Burj Khalifa, Aquaventure, Wild Wadi, Legoland, Motiongate, Ski Dubai, La Perle), Pool 2 the activities (iFly, the 24-hour City Sightseeing bus, a morning desert safari, kayak and speedboat tours) and Pool 3 the shorter visits (Lost World Aquarium, Dubai Frame, Madame Tussauds, The View at the Palm).

Here is the honest math. A typical first-timer trio, Aquaventure from Pool 1, the 24h hop-on hop-off bus from Pool 2 and the Lost World Aquarium from Pool 3, costs €128.02 bought separately (€76.96 for Aquaventure, €51.06 for the City Sightseeing bus-plus-aquarium ticket). That makes the pass €5.10 more expensive. It only pulls ahead if your Pool 2 pick is one of the pricier items, like iFly, the desert safari or the Marina sunset dinner cruise, whose single prices are not part of this comparison.

Who it suits: someone who wants one big ticket and two extras in a week and likes the structure. If you want two headliners, the pools block you; go for the Top Attractions Pass instead. The rating is 3.9 out of 5, with complaints mostly about attractions changing before travel.

review: This is the lightweight option: a 1, 2 or 3-day City Sightseeing hop-on hop-off ticket with Lost World Aquarium entry from €51.06. The two routes split the city cleanly. The Red Route (90 minutes) covers old Dubai: Al Seef, Al Fahidi, the Old Souk, the Gold and Spice Souk and the Dubai Frame. The Blue Route (130 minutes) heads to Madinat Jumeirah, Atlantis The Palm, Dubai Marina, JBR and Mall of the Emirates.

If you are in Dubai for one or two days, this one is enough; for longer stays, the 5-day pass is the better buy. For guided alternatives, see our Dubai city tours compared.

review: The SuperSaver is a different kind of pass. Instead of an app, the local operator MyPass UAE books your choices for you after checkout, via its team or WhatsApp. You pick 3, 5 or 7 from 23 options, valid 6, 7 or 8 days after first use. The list leans towards tours rather than parks: dhow dinner cruises on the Marina and the Creek with transfers, a desert safari with transfers, an Abu Dhabi tour, a luxury yacht tour and a 2-hour Marina sunset cruise, alongside Burj Khalifa Level 124, IMG Worlds, Dubai Frame, iFly, Ski Dubai and La Perle.

Use it for the wrong things and it costs you. Burj Khalifa (€69.01), IMG Worlds (€63.30) and the Dubai Frame (€13.03) add up to €145.34, which is €11.49 less than the €156.83 pass. Two guests say the same in their reviews: booked separately, it came out cheaper. The value sits in the transfer-included tours: an evening dhow dinner, the safari and the Abu Dhabi trip are the picks to build around (compare the safari against our desert safaris in Dubai before you commit).

At 4.3 out of 5 it is the best-rated of the pick-your-own passes, and the only one listed as wheelchair-accessible. It does not include Aquaventure, Wild Wadi or any Dubai Parks park, so families after water parks should look at #1.

review: The Unlimited pass flips the logic: pay €409.39 once, then visit as many of 35 attractions as you can in 3 or 5 consecutive days. The list overlaps heavily with the Top Attractions Pass (Burj Khalifa At the Top, Aquaventure, Lost World Aquarium, Wild Wadi, Legoland, Motiongate, Ski Dubai, iFly, La Perle) and adds Global Village, but IMG Worlds is not included.

The break-even is steep. Four of Dubai's most-booked tickets, Burj Khalifa (€69.01), Aquaventure (€76.96), the hop-on hop-off bus with Lost World Aquarium (€51.06) and the Dubai Frame (€13.03), total €210.06. That is barely half the pass price. To come out ahead in 3 days you need roughly twice that, which means two or three paid attractions every day, with the rule that 1 hour must pass between redemptions. One guest managed around 20 attractions in 5 days; most visitors will not.

The 3.2 out of 5 rating is the lowest of the Smartvisit passes, with complaints about the app (pending bookings, no language options). Book it only if you are sure you will run a packed schedule; for everyone else the 5 or 7-pick Top Attractions Pass is the safer value.

review: Go City's pass is the most flexible on paper: 3, 4, 5, 7 or 10 picks from 55+ attractions and tours across Dubai and Abu Dhabi, with 30 days to use them once the first one is scanned (and a year from purchase to start). The named list mixes aquariums (Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo, Lost Chambers), views (The View at The Palm, Sky Views, Dubai Frame), a desert safari with BBQ dinner, a Creek dhow dinner cruise, inside Burj Al Arab and an Abu Dhabi day trip.

At €173.24 for 3 picks you need about €57.75 of value per pick. Spend one on the €13.03 Dubai Frame and you are already behind. Burj Khalifa At the Top and Aquaventure are not on the named list, so this is not the pass for those two; it works best built around the safari, the Abu Dhabi trip and Burj Al Arab.

We rank it last for one reason: it has only 3 reviews, averaging 2.0 out of 5. Two reviewers describe bookings that did not operate or tickets that did not work, and one says it cost more than paying at each attraction. That is too little data to call it bad, but too much risk to put it ahead of passes with far longer review records. If you book it, reserve every attraction early in the app.

guide.h2: Dubai Attraction Passes Compared Side by Side
guide.html:
All seven passes on the numbers that decide whether a pass pays: price, number of picks, validity, the headline attractions on the list and a worked example against single tickets. Single-ticket prices used in the math: Burj Khalifa Level 124/125 €69.01, Atlantis Aquaventure €76.96, IMG Worlds €63.30, Dubai Frame €13.03 and the 1-day bus + Lost World Aquarium €51.06.

The pattern is clear. A pick-your-own pass saves money only when every pick is a big-ticket attraction; spend a pick on the €13 Dubai Frame and almost every pass loses. The one deal that wins without careful picking is the 5-day bus pass, because its included Frame and aquarium entries cost more separately than the pass itself.

guide.h2: Which Dubai Pass Should You Book?
guide.html:
• Burj Khalifa, Aquaventure and IMG Worlds on one trip: the Top Attractions Pass (3 picks saves €30.56; 5 or 7 picks if you add Ski Dubai, Legoland or iFly).
  • First visit, 4-5 days, no car, relaxed pace: the 5-day Big Bus pass, then buy a Burj Khalifa ticket separately.
  • One headliner plus two smaller extras: the Select pass, as long as your Pool 2 pick is iFly, the desert safari or the dinner cruise rather than the bus.
  • One or two days in Dubai: the City Sightseeing bus + aquarium at €51.
  • Evening dhow cruises, a desert safari and Abu Dhabi with transfers: the SuperSaver Pass.
  • Two or three paid attractions every day for 3-5 days: the Unlimited pass, and only then.
  • A month-long stay or Dubai plus Abu Dhabi: the Go City Highlights Pass, with the caveat of its very short review record.
  • Only one or two attractions in total: skip the passes and buy single tickets: our water parks and theme parks comparisons have the best single options.

guide.h2: Is a Dubai Pass Worth It? The Math
guide.html:
The 3-step test

1. Write down the paid attractions you would book anyway. 2. Add up their single prices. 3. Compare with the pass for the same number of picks. If the pass is not at least 10% cheaper, buy singles: they have no time windows, no pools and no app to manage.

Worked example: the big three

Burj Khalifa Level 124/125 (€69.01) + Atlantis Aquaventure (€76.96) + IMG Worlds (€63.30) = €209.27. On the Top Attractions Pass that trio costs €178.71, a saving of €30.56 (about 15%). The same three are not possible on the Select pass (Burj Khalifa and Aquaventure share Pool 1, and IMG is not listed), the Unlimited pass (no IMG) or the SuperSaver (no Aquaventure).

Worked example: the budget trio

Burj Khalifa (€69.01) + IMG Worlds (€63.30) + Dubai Frame (€13.03) = €145.34. The two passes that can hold this trio cost more for 3 picks: €156.83 (SuperSaver) and €178.71 (Top Attractions). With cheap attractions in the mix, singles win.

Worked example: bus days

The 1-day City Sightseeing bus with Lost World Aquarium is €51.06; add the Dubai Frame (€13.03) and you are at €64.09. The 5-day Big Bus pass with both attractions is €62.78. If you will use the bus on more than one day, the 5-day pass is the obvious buy.

guide.h2: Practical Tips: Booking Slots, Validity and Extras
guide.html:
Booking time slots

None of the pick-your-own passes is a walk-in ticket for everything. The Dubai Pass products need the Smartvisit app to reserve dates and time slots, Go City uses its own app, and the SuperSaver is booked through the provider's team or WhatsApp. Reserve Burj Khalifa and the parks first: they are the picks that make the pass pay.

When the clock starts

Validity runs from your first attraction, not from purchase: 7 consecutive days on the Top Attractions and Select passes, 3 or 5 on Unlimited, 6 to 8 on the SuperSaver, 30 on Go City. Plan the first redemption for the day your busy stretch begins.

What costs extra

None of the passes includes transport between attractions, except the tours on the SuperSaver that list transfers, and the two bus passes, where the bus is the transport. Meals, tips and optional extras are not included. Hotel pickup is not part of either bus pass.

Check the list before you pay

Every pass warns that attractions can change. Seasonal items such as Miracle Garden and Global Village close for part of the year, and guests on the Smartvisit passes report attractions leaving the list. Confirm your must-sees in the app the week you travel. Comparing a safari on its own? See our desert safaris in Dubai.

faqs.q: Is the Dubai Pass worth it?
faqs.a: Only if your picks are big-ticket attractions. Burj Khalifa (€69.01), Aquaventure (€76.96) and IMG Worlds (€63.30) cost €209.27 separately versus €178.71 on the 3-pick Top Attractions Pass, a €30.56 saving. Swap in cheaper picks like the Dubai Frame (€13.03) and single tickets come out cheaper.

faqs.q: Which Dubai attraction pass is best?
faqs.a: For Burj Khalifa, Aquaventure and IMG Worlds, the Dubai Top Attractions Pass (from €179, 7 days). For relaxed sightseeing, the 5-day Big Bus pass with Lost World Aquarium and Dubai Frame (€63), the best-rated option at 4.4 out of 5.

faqs.q: Go City Dubai vs Dubai Pass: which is better?
faqs.a: The Dubai Pass (Top Attractions, Select, Unlimited) includes Burj Khalifa At the Top and Aquaventure and has a longer review record (37 to 164 reviews per pass). The Go City Highlights Pass gives 30 days and adds Abu Dhabi and inside Burj Al Arab, but has only 3 reviews averaging 2.0 out of 5 and does not name Burj Khalifa or Aquaventure on its list.

faqs.q: Does a Dubai pass include Burj Khalifa?
faqs.a: The Top Attractions, Select, Unlimited and SuperSaver passes include Burj Khalifa (At the Top, or Level 124 on the SuperSaver). The two bus passes do not; pair them with a ticket from our Burj Khalifa tickets comparison.

faqs.q: Is the Dubai Unlimited Pass worth it?
faqs.a: Rarely. At €409.39 you need around €410 of tickets in 3 days. Burj Khalifa, Aquaventure, the bus with Lost World Aquarium and the Dubai Frame together are only €210.06, and there is a 1-hour gap rule between attractions. It is rated 3.2 out of 5 and does not include IMG Worlds.

faqs.q: How long is a Dubai attraction pass valid?
faqs.a: From the first attraction: 7 days for the Top Attractions and Select passes, 3 or 5 days for Unlimited, 6 to 8 days for the SuperSaver (by number of picks), 5 days for the Big Bus pass and 30 days for Go City. The City Sightseeing bus ticket covers 1, 2 or 3 days and can be used any day within 12 months.

No pick-your-own pass includes transport between attractions, apart from the SuperSaver tours that list transfers (dhow cruises, desert safari). The two hop-on hop-off passes are the transport, covering Downtown, the Creek souks, Madinat Jumeirah, Atlantis and the Marina.

methodology: We compared 7 bookable Dubai attraction passes: four pick-your-own passes from the Dubai Pass and MyPass ranges, Go City's Highlights Pass and two hop-on hop-off bundles with attraction entry. Each was scored on from-price, number of picks, validity, which headline attractions are on the list, booking method and ratings, then priced against single tickets for Burj Khalifa, Aquaventure, IMG Worlds, the Dubai Frame and the 1-day bus with Lost World Aquarium to show where a pass saves money and where it does not. Prices are live adult from-prices for a normal date; ratings come from verified guest reviews.
